description: This course examines how 19th-century Russian male authors and critics used the "woman question"
to debate broader ethical, societal, and political issues. The course analyzes how these men
defined ethical living in an autocratic empire, often erasing female voices from the discourse.
Students read major works by Pushkin, Leskov, and Tolstoy, evaluating ethical perspectives while
reflecting on the historical marginalization of women in Russian literary culture. (Taught in
Russian) Offered periodically. Prerequisite: RUSSN 302 or permission from the instructor.
fullname: The Heroine in Russian Literature (Taught in Russian)
